summary: Module 3 BREAK: silent data corruption race found and fixed. The canonical last_accessed_at stale-timestamp bug is structurally absent in this fork (clicks are event-sourced rows with per-click clicked_at; analytics derives last_clicked_at = max(clicked_at), so no shared timestamp column can go stale). The same race class -- concurrent read-then-write leaving silently stale state, correct counts, zero errors -- exists in the redirect cache: _resolve_with_cache reads DB then populates cache, while update_link commits then invalidates; a stale populate landing after invalidation serves the OLD URL until TTL. Deterministically reproduced with an interleaved repro (read old -> update+invalidate -> stale populate) and observed via live redirect: 302 to old URL when DB has new URL. Fixed with a generation/version token in cache.py: invalidate_redirect_target INCRs redirect:ver:<code> before deleting, set_redirect_target captures the version before the DB read and WATCH-pipelines a conditional populate (skips if version changed), get_redirect_target rejects payloads whose version mismatches. Repro now serves the new URL; added regression test test_stale_populate_after_invalidate_is_rejected; full suite 73 tests pass; server restarted and healthy.
